corrected_row: | DOC-A.1-6 | **Alignment of alphanumeric group items (and strongly-typed group items) relative to the first item within the group**, §8.5.1.6.1 · §8.5.1.6.5, required + documented | **Always coincident.** Every alphanumeric group item, and every strongly-typed group item (a group declared by a `TYPEDEF STRONG` type, 2002 onward), starts at the same byte as the first item subordinate to it, whatever that item's class or usage: COBOL.NET never places slack bytes ahead of a group's first item, and none between items either (no automatic alignment, item 7; no alignment or implicit FILLER for SYNCHRONIZED, item 195) — the only implicit filler is the filler bits §8.5.1.6.3 itself requires after a bit data item to reach the next byte (`05 B1 PIC 1(3) USAGE BIT` followed by `05 B2 PIC X` is a 2-byte group). A group of byte-sized items is therefore exactly the sum of its subordinate items' sizes: `05 G1 PIC 9(4) COMP` followed by `05 G2 PIC X` is a 3-byte group whose first two bytes are G1, and a strongly-typed group of `9(4) COMP-5` then `X` is likewise 3 bytes. The standard's own exceptions (the group coincident with a first item that is national, boolean, message-tag, object or pointer; the type's essential characteristics preserved) hold because there is no other case. The same answer at every edition; one layout authority computes every offset and size (`RecordLayout.OffsetOf`, `RecordLayout.PhysicalWidth`). | — |

corrected_record.notes: Row written from the code: RecordLayout.PhysicalWidth sums subordinate widths with no padding term and OffsetOf advances by the same widths, so every group (alphanumeric or strongly-typed) is coincident with its first item. No spec-derived golden pins the group-start offset directly (test-ref empty; row says —). 8.5.1.6.5 applies from 2002; 8.5.1.6.1 at every edition. Owning note: A11 umbrella / PB1522 step 3.

corrected_row: | DOC-A.1-7 | **Alignment of data for increased object-code efficiency (special or automatic alignment, implicit filler, semantics of statements)**, §8.5.1.6.4 · §13.18.55.4 GR10, optional (documented if provided) | **Not provided.** COBOL.NET provides no special type of alignment and specifies no automatic alignment: every item sits immediately after its predecessor with no implicit FILLER (other than the filler bits §8.5.1.6.3 requires after a bit data item, which is not alignment for efficiency), with or without the SYNCHRONIZED clause (whose own effect is item 195), so no statement sees a group differently because of alignment — `05 PIC X`, `05 PIC S9(9) COMP-5`, `05 PIC X`, `05 COMP-2` is a 14-byte group at every edition (`RecordLayout.PhysicalWidth`). | — |

corrected_row: | DOC-A.1-16 | **CALL statement — calling a non-COBOL program**, §14.9.4.4 GR3g, required + documented | **Not possible: COBOL.NET executes no non-COBOL program through CALL.** A CALL resolves only to a COBOL.NET program — one in the run unit, or a separately compiled COBOL.NET module `<program-name>.dll` in the application directory that carries the COBOL.NET module registrar (`ProgramTable.ProbeSiblingModule`). Every other target, including a .NET assembly that is present in the application directory (`CALL "Antlr4.Runtime.Standard"`) or a system library name held in an identifier, is **not located**, so GR3g's non-COBOL branch is never reached: the CALL is unsuccessful with **EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND** (GR3b) and continues per GR3h — the ON EXCEPTION imperative statement when one is written (ON OVERFLOW before 2023); otherwise, with checking for EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND enabled, the applicable exception declarative (item 17), and with checking not enabled (and always at 85) the run unit terminates abnormally naming EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND. There is no CALL-CONVENTION directive (§7.3.9), so a program cannot be declared non-COBOL either (item 19); program-name formation and locating for non-COBOL programs (items 13 and 15) therefore never arise. The same at every edition. | — |

Corrected one imprecise clause: 'otherwise the exception processing of item 17' covers only the checking-enabled case (GR3h2); with checking off (GR3h3 -> §14.6.13.1.3 #8) and at 85 the code terminates the run unit abnormally, which the row now says. cite 14.9.4.4 GR3g OK = A.1 cross-ref; ProbeSiblingModule symbol present; no pin claimed; record unchanged.
